claims.text: Bulgaria mid-10th c., priest Bogomil; dualism "imported especially from the Paulicians" plus Slavonic reform; material world made by the devil; rejected incarnation, baptism, Eucharist, Orthodox organisation; condemned marriage, meat, wine; councils; spread in Byzantium 11th–12th c.; c. 1100 Basil publicly burned; west late 12th c.; network Black Sea to Atlantic; faded after Ottoman conquest

katharos "pure"; two principles, material world evil; perfect and believers, consolamentum; organised church from 1140s, 11 bishoprics by c. 1200; criticized "worldliness and corruption"; Montségur 1244; hierarchy faded 1270s; disappeared early 15th c.

claims.text: "Intent upon the acquisition of temporal power, it had well-nigh abandoned its spiritual duties."; clergy "accustomed to conceal the tonsure through very shame"; Cathars rejected tithes and oblations

claims.text: 1209–1229; Raymond VI implicated in legate murder; Innocent III March 1208 "a Crusade against Raymond and the heretics of Languedoc"; indulgence, at most 40 days; popular in north; Béziers 1209 massacre; Lateran IV 1215 lands to Simon de Montfort; Montfort killed at Toulouse; Louis VIII 1226; 1229 lands to Capetians, "the French crown the ultimate victor"; Inquisition virtually eliminated Catharism within a century

Caesarius of Heisterbach: "Caedite eos. Novit enim Dominus qui sunt eius", "dixisse fertur"; Barber: "usually (although not invariably) discounted by serious historians"; Amalric letter Aug 1209: spared no one "irrespective of rank, sex, or age", almost 20,000 killed; population 10,000–14,500

May 1243 – 16 March 1244; Hugues des Arcis ~10,000 vs ~100; Pierre-Roger de Mirepoix "protected a community of Cathars"; all could leave "except those who would not renounce their Cathar faith"; about 210 burned; Avignonet 28 May 1242 two Inquisition representatives killed

"led lives of religious devotion without joining an approved religious order"; beguinages; nursing, cloth, lace; chastity while in community; ties to friars and mysticism led to suspicion; Council of Vienne 1311 decrees ordering dissolution; toleration from 15th c.; communities remain in Belgium

Beguine; Mirror of Simple Souls, "Annihilated Soul", "given up everything except God through Love"; 1296–1306 burned at Valenciennes in her presence; William of Paris; refused to speak, recant, take oath; relapsed heretic; "burnt alive on 1 June 1310 in Paris", Place de Grève; circulated anonymously, Latin, Italian, Middle English; Ad Nostrum 1311 cited extracts; Guarnieri 1946

c. 1501–1700; soul "having attained a certain degree of perfection"; "entered into direct communication with the Holy Spirit"; free of liturgy, good works, exterior forms; from reformed Franciscans and Jesuits; all classes; edicts 1568, 1574, 1623
Co-founder of Alumbrados; seamstress of Guadalajara; family "descended from New Christians"; trial 1524–1529; jailed after auto de fe; influenced Ruiz de Alcaraz, María de Cazalla

1628–1696; Spiritual Guide Rome 1675, "caused a sensation"; arrested 1685 under his friend Innocent XI; life imprisonment for heresy; 68 propositions condemned 1687; admitted being wrong; died in prison
